html:
In the app

Guided mode’s lesson 5 is this chapter: it checks that this lesson’s tags are made, that S3_Index exists, is called from MainRoutine and verifies, and then watches the line while you run it and ticks each result as it happens:

  • The belt steps one pitch (Conv_Index)
  • Bottles walk down the line: three dropped, one at every stop

This is the step that makes it a line, and it comes third because every station after it needs bottles to arrive. The belt must move exactly one pitch and stop: the encoder on Main_Conv gives one rising edge of channel A per 40 px, so the rule is latch Conv_Index, run the belt, unlatch on the next edge. Add JSR(S3_Index); to MainRoutine under step 2. From now on it stays the last JSR: each station you add in the lessons that follow goes above it (guided mode’s Add it puts it there, and says so if one ends up below).

Tags this lesson needs

Create these before you type the rungs (Verify reports any you miss as unknown). Tags from earlier lessons are not repeated.

TagTypeKindDescription

LS7BOOLalias of Local:1:I.Data.13LogixPro I:1/12 · Cap ram down

Main_Conv_ABOOLalias of Local:1:I.Data.2Main_Conv encoder channel A: one rising edge per 40 px pitch

The rungs

How it fits together

Rung 0 starts a step: the line runs, the dwell is done, no fill, cap, label or inspection is in progress (the request bits are off), and neither the tube (LS4) nor the ram (LS7) is down. Those stations do not exist yet, so their bits are 0 and the rung passes; it is written complete now so it never has to be revisited. Rung 1 resets step 2’s dwell while the belt steps. Rung 2 runs the motor only while stepping and only while the line runs. Rung 3 ends the step: the next rising edge of encoder A unlatches Conv_Index, and the ONS sits right after Main_Conv_A so it tracks the encoder, not the step. A Stop in the middle of a step leaves Conv_Index latched and stops the motor; Start runs the motor again and the step ends on the same encoder edge it would have, one pitch from where it began. That is what keeps the registers and the bottles together.

Why JSR(S3_Index) is the last JSR. Rung 0 looks at the fill, cap, label and inspection requests, and those are decided in their own routines, in the same scan, from Dwell.DN. If S3_Index ran first it would latch the step in the scan the dwell finished, before the filler had asked to hold the belt, and the bottle would leave the filler empty. Scanned last, it sees every request first.

Run it

Start the line. The belt steps, stops, a bottle drops, a second passes, the belt steps. Bottles walk down the line one pitch at a time and are removed at the end. Nothing fills, caps or sorts them yet: the lessons that follow add one station at a time, and each one works as soon as it is written because the bottles are already arriving.

Try it

Change the Dwell preset to 300 ms and watch the line speed up without losing a bottle. Set it back to 1000.

rungs.head: S3_Index · Rung 0
rungs.comment: START THE STEP once the dwell is done, the tube (LS4) and ram (LS7) are up, and no fill, cap or label is in progress
rungs.words: When Line_Run (Seal-in run bit (LogixPro B3:0/0)) is on, Dwell.DN (the done bit of Dwell: Belt stopped: sensors read, feeder drops a bottle) is on, LS4 (LogixPro I:1/9 · Fill tube down) is off, LS7 (LogixPro I:1/12 · Cap ram down) is off, Fill_Req (A bottle stands under the filler and still needs its charge) is off, Cap_Req (A bottle stands under the cap ram and has not been capped) is off, Label_Req (Latched while the labeler is asked to apply; cleared at PadIn) is off and Insp_Req (An inspection is under way: triggered, no result yet (holds the belt)) is off, the rung latches Conv_Index (Latched while the belt steps one pitch) on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Line_Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Line_Run is on.
  2. XIC(Dwell.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when Dwell.DN is on.
  3. XIO(LS4) Examine If Open asks: true when LS4 is off.
  4. XIO(LS7) Examine If Open asks: true when LS7 is off.
  5. XIO(Fill_Req) Examine If Open asks: true when Fill_Req is off.
  6. XIO(Cap_Req) Examine If Open asks: true when Cap_Req is off.
  7. XIO(Label_Req) Examine If Open asks: true when Label_Req is off.
  8. XIO(Insp_Req) Examine If Open asks: true when Insp_Req is off.
  9. OTL(Conv_Index) Output Latch does: latches Conv_Index on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Conv_Index stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.
pats.think: a light switch rather than a doorbell: flick it on and it stays on until someone flicks it off.
pats.watch: A latched bit survives a stop, and it survives a download that keeps tag values. If nothing ever unlatches it, the machine remembers a state that is long gone.

rungs.head: S3_Index · Rung 1
rungs.comment: The belt is stepping: reset the dwell for the next stop. A retentive timer only clears with RES

pred.q: Conv_Index is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Dwell is reset.

rungs.words: When Conv_Index (Latched while the belt steps one pitch) is on, the rung resets Dwell (Belt stopped: sensors read, feeder drops a bottle).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Conv_Index) Examine If Closed asks: true when Conv_Index is on.
  2. RES(Dwell) Reset does: resets Dwell. It zeroes a timer or counter (accumulator and status bits), or a control (its position and status bits).

rungs.head: S3_Index · Rung 2
rungs.comment: RUN THE BELT only while stepping and the line runs: a step cut short by Stop (or a fault) stays latched and finishes after Start

pred.q: Line_Run is off and Conv_Index is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Main_Conveyor is off. It stops at XIC(Line_Run).

rungs.words: When Line_Run (Seal-in run bit (LogixPro B3:0/0)) is on and Conv_Index (Latched while the belt steps one pitch) is on, the rung turns Main_Conveyor (LogixPro O:2/0 · Main conveyor motor) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Line_Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Line_Run is on.
  2. XIC(Conv_Index) Examine If Closed asks: true when Conv_Index is on.
  3. OTE(Main_Conveyor) Output Energize does: turns Main_Conveyor on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: S3_Index · Rung 3
rungs.comment: END THE STEP on the next rising edge of encoder A, which is exactly one 40 px pitch. The ONS sits right after Main_Conv_A so it tracks the encoder, not the step. Try it: change Dwell to 300 ms and watch the line speed up without losing a bottle
rungs.words: When Main_Conv_A (Main_Conv encoder channel A: one rising edge per 40 px pitch) is on, this is the first scan of it and Conv_Index (Latched while the belt steps one pitch) is on, the rung unlatches Conv_Index.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Main_Conv_A) Examine If Closed asks: true when Main_Conv_A is on.
  2. ONS(A_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in A_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  3. XIC(Conv_Index) Examine If Closed asks: true when Conv_Index is on.
  4. OTU(Conv_Index) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Conv_Index. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.
pats.think: a turnstile. However long you stand in it, it counts you once.
pats.watch: Each one-shot needs its own storage bit. Two one-shots sharing a bit fight over it, and one of them never fires.
